title: The first computer bug
alt: A page of the Harvard Mark II logbook dated 9/9. A moth is taped beside the 15:45 entry, Relay #70 Panel F (moth) in relay, above the note: First actual case of bug being found.
author: Courtesy of the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Dahlgren, VA., 1988.
credit: U.S. Naval Historical Center Online Library Photograph NH 96566-KN The above link is no longer valid on 13.04.2017, the image available here.
description: The First "Computer Bug" Moth found trapped between points at Relay # 70, Panel F, of the Mark II Aiken Relay Calculator while it was being tested at Harvard University, 9 September 1947. The operators affixed the moth to the computer log, with the entry: "First actual case of bug being found". (The term "debugging" already existed; thus, finding an actual bug was an amusing occurrence.) In 1988, the log, with the moth still taped by the entry, was in the Naval Surface Warfare Center Computer Museum at Dahlgren, Virginia, which erroneously dated it 9 September 1945.
